Just to note: When you have waterfowl, you want to introduce them to the water early. The earlier they are in the faster (and better) their oil gland will develop. Water fowl in the wild can go into the water extremely early (the gosling I rescued was not even 24 hours old, we assume her parents had built their nest RIGHT on the river we live next to). But do not let them swim by themselves!!!

When you start them out, start them in water they can stand in. Their oil glands won't develop for some time and it's that oil that makes their feathers water resistant and helps keep them buoyant. If they have parents, the parents will oil them. As they get older and stronger they can go into deeper water, but again, do not leave them alone. Once their pin feathers come in is about the time you can let them have swim time without you needing to watch over them. But make sure they have easy access in and out of the pool.
